A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical DRO research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the newly added Appendix I in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on CMNIST, Waterbirds, and CelebA, including minority-group shifts, corrected Waterbirds labels, perturbation-radius sensitivity, and Grad-CAM analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments with standard Wasserstein DRO on shifted Waterbirds and CelebA in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The hierarchical ambiguity set, latent-space perturbations, group-dependent radii, Algorithm 1 updates, and tuning procedure are unchanged. Expanded explanations of these choices do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same original and shifted CMNIST, Waterbirds, and CelebA tasks, including corrected Waterbirds. Appendix I reuses existing minority-shift scenarios without adding datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix I newly evaluates standard Wasserstein DRO against the hierarchical approach. Figure 14 also introduces ERM reference results for shifted Waterbirds and CelebA; v1 reports ERM only in the original-distribution comparison. Existing comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix I comparison sweeps standard Wasserstein DRO's global radius while specifying the same latent-space cost and training hyperparameters as the proposed method. Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and tuning procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a diagnostic radius sweep testing whether a single unconditional Wasserstein ball provides robustness comparable to the hierarchical construction. The existing perturbation sensitivity, t-SNE examples, label-correction comparison, and Grad-CAM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-run reporting, table uncertainties, and Figure 11 standard-deviation bands are unchanged. The new Figure 14 supplies no additional run-count information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figure 14 adds standard Wasserstein DRO accuracy curves and shifted ERM reference levels. The new baseline's worst-group accuracy peaks at approximately 40% on Waterbirds and 30% on CelebA, below the retained hierarchical results of 93.7% and 72.1%. Tables 1–3 and earlier result figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, Proposition B.1, their proofs, and Appendix C's derivation are unchanged; the fixed-feature assumption already appears in v1. The added tightness remark repeats Appendix A's inequality and supplies a heuristic density-based interpretation, without a new formal bound or revised proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical uncertainty, tractable optimization, and robustness to minority-group shifts. Appendix I provides additional support for the existing contribution rather than redefining it.

C2.justification: v2 explains the choices of unrestricted group proportions and Wasserstein uncertainty, discusses possible relaxation strictness and expected near-tightness, and explicitly limits the convergence guarantee to fixed representations. Appendix I adds interpretations attributing standard DRO's weakness to missing group-proportion uncertainty and group-specific radii.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly supplies a code-repository link. Appendix I documents matching latent costs and training hyperparameters for its added comparison. Previously reported hardware, architecture, optimization settings, and hyperparameter grids are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Kim et al. (2026), connecting spurious correlations to failures of domain adaptation. The expanded discussion further distinguishes the approach from standard Wasserstein and f-divergence DRO, while retaining the existing references and overall positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory paragraphs in Section 4 and Appendix B, Appendix I, acknowledgments, and corresponding-author and conference text. Most prose and the existing section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Figure 14 and conference headers, with reflow and relocation of Algorithm 1, Table 3, and some appendix material. Existing Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–3 retain their content and display designs.

improvement.justification: Appendix I supplies a relevant empirical control missing from v1, while the code pointer and explicit explanation of the convergence guarantee's limited scope improve reproducibility information and clarity. These are limited gains: the method and established results remain unchanged, Figure 14 lacks uncertainty reporting, and the new near-tightness argument remains heuristic rather than demonstrated.
